newsitem.title: JAPAN: MOF says told to limit general budget spending.
newsitem.headline: MOF says told to limit general budget spending.

text.p: Japanese Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka was told by Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto on Tuesday to limit general spending in the overall fiscal budget for next year, a ministry official told reporters.
The official said the general spending was expected to have grown 2.4 percent in the budget for the current fiscal year.

"We were told to limit grow substantially. The finance minister took that instruction from the prime minister to mean the growth rate (in general spending) would be between one and two percent," the official said.
General spending, the core of the budget, totalled 43.14 trillion yen in the original budget for the fiscal year to next March.
The total budget for the 1996/97 fiscal year totalled 75.10 trillion yen.
Hashimoto asked Mitsuzuka to review overall spending without exceptions, including defence-related costs and aid to other countries, the official said.
Hashimoto also asked the finance minister to reduce the size of the government's general loans and investment programme.
The programme, funded by postal insurance, postal savings and other public funds, is separate from the main budget.
The programme totalled 40.54 trillion yen in the current fiscal year, up 0.7 percent from the 1995/96 fiscal year.

The MOF official said that as implementing a planned consumption tax increase from three to five percent from April 1 would boost government spending by about one percent that would already put overall spending growth into the range which the ministry feels it should not exceed.
